safetyRegulatoryGates: Resort written permission (not obtained; gate for every concept)
G-MATURE closed; nothing physically tested (M-070 not_run)
Resort written permission is a hard gate: most resorts prohibit kites/tethered objects on pistes; the line at 0.9–1.5 m above snow behind the rider is a clothesline hazard (A2-K2-04).
Canopy/line dragged on the snow at rider speed in 10/39 runs (A2-K2-03): trip/snag hazard to others; must be eliminated by design.
KE 14.73 J vs 14.9 J line (FAA Part 107 Cat 2 reference) with 1.2 % margin; rider >14.6 m/s → 16.8 J during auto-dock.
Lift interlock relies on an ASSUMED on-snow vibration signature for down-riding chairlifts.
Kite at ≤7 m line, ≤≈10 m AGL: generally outside drone rules but subject to local kite/tethered-object rules near lifts and power lines.

majorFindings.title: Pass threshold on canopy L/D is ≥1.0, not ≥≈0.9 as claimed
Dock-funnel acceptance of 120° off-axis is load-bearing for setupTime and ops
Canopy lands and is dragged over the snow at rider speed, then re-inflates unreefed (snatch)
Line 0.9–1.5 m above snow 1 m behind the rider in every ensemble run (own gate ≥2.0 m)
Continuous actuated reefing + glide while reefed has no precedent

concepts.credibleEnvelope: Simulation-credible only for: empty or low-traffic piste with written permission, rider 8–14 m/s carving, wind 0–9 m/s head/cross or calm (tail ≥6 m/s degrades to 70–81 %), AND a canopy that tow-tests at L/D ≥1.0 unreefed with ≥70 % glide kept when reefed, a ≤86 g flying mass, and a dock that captures from ≥120° off-axis. Each of those is unmeasured; with MC1-1C-class glide (0.75) or a 90° funnel it fails.
concepts.auditVerdict: Reproduces exactly (39/39) and passes all judged metrics as modelled (independent avail 85.2 %, setup p90 24.0 s, ops p90 2/max 3, F 30.4 N, KE 14.73 J, endurance 85 min). But the pass is knife-edge and conditional: the stated L/D threshold is wrong (needs ≥1.0, not ≈0.9), docking acceptance and reefed glide are load-bearing and unprecedented, relift snatches are under-read, and the line height behind the rider is an unfixed bystander hazard. Rank as a high-risk research concept, not a credible usable product, until tow tests settle polar/reefing/docking.

concepts.auditVerdict: Reproduces exactly (0 differences on all 39 cases). Judged on the shared ensemble: FAIL avail (61.4 %, 72.5 % even for launched runs), FAIL/at-risk jitter on the integrator metric (p90 3.4 °/s), likely FAIL packVol (≈4 L); pass pxMed, azRange, addedMass, bodyForce, handsBusy, setupTime, ops, keMax, endurance (thin margin on line resistance). Safety gap: slow rider + light tailwind inside the gate gives stall, snow contact and a 0.78 m helmet pass. Best of the four gliders on operations (1 action, ~11 s standstill) but not a usable solo follow-cam as specified.

Resort written permission (gate for every concept); a glider landing ahead on the piste at every stop and at the lift approach is an obstacle for other skiers (dev Poisson estimate: ≈2.1 passes within 5 m of the flying glider per run at medium density before avoidance).
EU: 168.5 g < 250 g → C0/Open A1; follow-me ≤50 m enforced by a 48 m hard limit, but violated (72–141 m) if the launch gate misjudges a ≥6 m/s downslope wind.

US: recreational/Part 107 VLOS — the glider flies ahead of the rider within ≤48 m, so the rider can see it more easily than a chase drone, but the rider is also the pilot while skiing; Part 107 Cat 1 over people requires <0.55 lb AND no exposed rotating parts that can lacerate (pusher prop exposed).
Pusher prop + 0.76 m wing at up to 14.6 J; touchdown slides up to 8.5 m (17 m on ice).

concepts.credibleEnvelope: Groomed piste, mean wind ≤6 m/s and downslope ≤3 m/s, rider ≤13 m/s, launch gate working, AND pointing error ≲2° (better than UWB PDoA spec): avail ≈82–89 %. Outside that (≥6 m/s tailwind, 9 m/s, powder, ice, UWB-only pointing at ±5°) it fails or does not fly.
concepts.auditVerdict: Numbers reproduce exactly (0 diffs). Judged avail fails (64.6 %); setup, ops, force, KE (marginal 0.3 J), endurance pass. Inside its envelope it is the only head-on concept and is credible as a light-wind niche product, conditional on a better-than-UWB pointing source, robust snow take-off and a non-oracle wind gate; KE/50 m compliance is gate-dependent.

endurance.conceptAuditNote: per-run accounting (flight energy throw→rest + 0.6 W heater over the whole 6 min lift; only riding minutes count as filming) gives 66.5 min — still ≥45. Flying cell 2 Wh → ≈9 runs at the mean, recharge 1.1–1.6 C on the lift needs a warm (>10 °C) cell, more than the 0.6 W heater budget is shown to deliver (unverified).

massBudget.note: components.js: cam4k 16 + avionics 10 + 5 servos 12.5 + motorProp 11 + wiring 5 = 54.5 g shared items; explicit ASSUMED ToF 5 g, cradle 5 g, airframe 30 g, 2 Wh cell 13.3 g (150 Wh/kg) → 107.8 g ×1.15 = 124.0 g — arithmetic reproduced, <250 g (C0 mass OK). Airframe 30 g for a 0.065 m² folding wing with pod, hinge and spiked skid that must survive belly landings and 6–12 J snow strikes is optimistic; at 40 g airframe → 135.5 g, KE-cap speed 14.8 m/s; dev sensitivity +15 g → light-wind avail 75→65 %.

safetyRegulatoryGates: Resort written permission (not obtained; gate for every concept)
G-MATURE closed; nothing physically tested (M-070 not_run)
EU: 124 g (<250 g) can be C0-class; C0 follow-me must stay ≤50 m from the remote pilot (2019/945 Part 1) — breached once (69.8 m) in the ensemble; A1 follow-me height ≤50 m.
US: Part 107/recreational rules require VLOS by the operator or a visual observer; a skier facing downhill cannot watch a glider behind them — no legal US solo operation without a waiver.
Resort written permission (gate for every concept); many resorts ban drones outright.
Landing at the lift approach (the most crowded spot) every run; no bystander detection in the landing logic beyond the rider.
Pusher prop near the hand at throw; snow strikes at 6–12 J.

ranking.question: usable solo follow-cam (self-operated, full run, real winds, minimal set-up)
ranking.summary: No round-2 concept is a usable solo follow-cam as specified: leapfrog, towglider and descentglider fail the judged full-ensemble avail; kite2 passes only on unproven canopy/dock physics and carries an unjudged line hazard. Ranking is by credible usable envelope × evidence, not by count of passes.

order.label: best credible light-wind follow-cam; fails the all-weather avail
order.rationale: Reproduces exactly; fails only avail on the full ensemble (64.4 %), and that failure is an honest operating limit (it refuses to launch in ≥6 m/s tail / strong wind) rather than a footage defect: 84 % over all flown runs, 87–88 % at 0–3 m/s. All other 11 metrics pass on the harmonised basis (jitter p90 1.0 °/s, setup 14–25 s, ops 2, KE 14.6 J). Conventional technology (small glider, post reframing). Conditions: pointing better than UWB spec (≲2°), a real (non-oracle) wind gate, robust snow take-off, KE margin only 0.3 J, landing ahead of the rider at every stop, US VLOS issue.

order.label: only concept passing all 12 as modelled, but the least evidenced and with an unjudged line hazard
order.rationale: Passes every judged metric on the audit basis (avail 85.2 %, setup 24 s, ops 2, F 30 N, KE 14.73 J, endurance 85 min) in all wind bins. But the pass sits on three unprecedented, load-bearing assumptions (slot-open L/D ≥1.0 — not ≈0.9 as claimed; ≥70 % of glide kept while reefed to ≈29 % drag area; 120° off-axis soft-canopy dock capture), a 0.17 J KE margin, unproven snatch forces, and a line 0.9–1.5 m above the snow behind the rider in every run plus canopy dragged on snow — a clothesline/trip hazard that most resorts will not permit. Highest upside if a tow test confirms glide/reefing/docking; not usable until then.

order.label: lowest operating burden, structurally capped footage
order.rationale: Best convenience (ops 1, setup 11 s, F ≤11 N, KE 12.9 J, credible 48 V leash at ≈0.26 g/m and 0.56 W loss). But avail is ≈72 % even in launched runs in every wind bin (launch-to-station and stop-drop/relaunch time), the shared jitter metric fails (p90 3.4 °/s; 8 % EIS residual assumed), packVol ≈4.2 L, rider-speed envelope ≤≈11 m/s on ≤15–18°, and near-helmet passes (0.78–0.9 m) in calm/slow tailwind. Fixing avail needs a different stop strategy, not tuning.

order.label: fails; calm-day no-line research niche only
order.rationale: Fails avail (29.6 %), setup (60 s; 33–35 s even calm), ops p90 3, KE 18 J, harmonised jitter (p90 18 °/s); near misses and landings beside the rider inside its ≤3 m/s envelope, one 50 m geofence breach. Dominated by towglider on setup, ops, KE and windy avail; wins only calm-air avail (87 vs 72 %) and needs no line.
